title: What If the World Ran Out of Helium?

scenes.text: What if the world ran out of helium? Party balloons are the least of it.
Helium comes from deep underground and can't be manufactured.
Once it's released, it drifts up and escapes into space for good.
Its biggest job is cooling MRI magnets to minus 269 degrees Celsius. A high-field scanner uses hundreds of liters.
Helium has the lowest boiling point of any element, so nothing else replaces it easily.
Balloons use about ten percent of it. The scanners are the real cost of running out.

description:
What if the world ran out of helium?
It can't be manufactured, it escapes into space, and it keeps hospital MRI magnets near absolute zero.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: What everyday thing would you be shocked to lose? Drop your 'what if'.
